# WordPress answers recorded on the bench

Each file is one answer of a WordPress 7.1.4 site to a request the module's password route makes: `what` was asked, the HTTP `status`, the `headers` the module reads (`Location`, `Link`, `Content-Type`, `Set-Cookie`, `WWW-Authenticate`, only those that were present) and the whole `body` (decoded JSON for JSON answers, otherwise the text). Recorded on 10 November 2026, run `S-20261110T091455`, against a throwaway WordPress site in containers, at `https://mainwp-bench-site.test/`.

Replaced before saving: every `Set-Cookie` value is `[bench]` (name and attributes kept), the REST nonce in `rest-nonce.json` is `0123abcd45`, every `_wpnonce` value is `abcdef0123`, and Two Factor's `wp-auth-nonce` value is `[bench]`. No request is kept, so no password; the script refuses to keep a file that holds a site password or the bench's dashboard key. HTML bodies are otherwise whole, for the marker tests.

The login-obstacle files (`llar-*`, `loginizer-*`, `aios-*`, `recaptcha-*`, `two-factor-*`, `wordfence-*`, `renamed-login-page`, `rest-index-wordfence`) were each recorded on a clean site with that one plugin from wordpress.org. `logout-confirm.json` is a 403 answer that holds the logout link.

The key-route files (`approve-*`, `key-*`, `rest-index-keys-off`, `rest-index-wordfence-keys-on`, `http-auth-*`) were recorded on 10 November 2026, runs `SK-20261110T102948` and `SK-20261110T103156`, by the same script's `key`, `keyforbidden`, `keywordfence`, `keyoff` and `httpauth` sections. They used the module's own values: `app_name` `WordPress Care`, `app_id` `7f1c2b8e-4d1a-4c47-9a53-2f6c0e8d1b10`, `success_url` `https://whmcs.bench.test/index.php?m=mainwp&mainwp_return=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef` and `reject_url` the same with `&mainwp_rejected=1`, and the care account `wpcare-k7m2x9`. The key was sent as HTTP Basic authentication (`user_login` and the application password). The application password in `approve-redirect.json` is replaced by `BenchKey0123456789ABCDEF`. In `approve-redirect-browser.json` it is replaced by `Benc%20hKey%200123%204567%2089AB%20CDEF`, in the encoding the browser used for the spaces. That file is the URL headless Chromium navigated to after the page's own `POST /wp/v2/users/me/application-passwords` (its 201 is the status kept); there is no HTTP redirect on that path, and the body is empty. `key-users-me-wordfence.json` and `key-user-create-wordfence.json` are kept because they differ from the plain site's answers (six extra Wordfence capabilities; a 400 `pass` for a password without a symbol). `http-auth-*` are Apache's answers, not WordPress's. The script refuses to keep a file holding the key in any form, its base64 Basic value, a care password or the HTTP-authentication password.

Changed after recording, on 10 November 2026, when the module was renamed: in every file the bench's host names (`wpcare-bench-site.test`, `wpcare-bench-dash.test`) became `mainwp-bench-site.test` and `mainwp-bench-dash.test`, the module's address and parameters in the approval's return address (`m=wpcare`, `wpcare_return`, `wpcare_rejected`) became `m=mainwp`, `mainwp_return` and `mainwp_rejected`, and the hash in the login cookies' names became the one WordPress derives from the new address. The same holds for `../mainwp/`. Nothing else was touched; where a file's `what` says a value is "exactly as sent", it is as sent but for those names.

Made by hand, not recorded, on 13 November 2026 from a real case seen that morning (a folder address with no WordPress of its own was accepted and stored): `folder-without-wordpress.json` (WordPress answers any path of the site with its 404 page and the main site's `Link` header), `home-wordpress-in-folder.json` and `rest-index-wordpress-in-folder.json` (a WordPress installed in the folder `/blog`, its index cut to the fields the module reads). Their `what` says so; nothing in them was sent by a real site.

Re-record from a running bench (`up.sh`, then `record-site.sh`); the cookie name hash, the site URL and the times will be the bench's again.
